text: In a cloud session with two repositories, each repo's CLAUDE.md, unscoped rules, skills, agents and commands load. Its hooks, permissions and other settings, its .mcp.json connectors and the plugins it turns on do not.
CLAUDE.md from both repos is paid on every request and loaded by every sub-agent unless the agent sets omitClaudeMd. Imports do not reduce the cost. Anthropic advises keeping it under 200 lines.
A skill costs only its name and description until it is used; the body loads on invocation as a message, so the cache holds. Description plus when_to_use is truncated at 1,536 characters.

On a subscription within plan usage, the main conversation's prompt cache lasts one hour; sub-agents, workflows and forks get five minutes. On usage credits the main conversation drops to five minutes.

These break the prompt cache: switching model (including a skill naming another model or a safety fallback), toggling fast mode, adding or removing MCP servers, compaction. These keep it: changing effort, invoking skills, spawning sub-agents, editing repo files.
Editing CLAUDE.md mid-session keeps the cache but does not apply until /clear, /compact or a restart.

A sub-agent's model resolves in this order: the per-call model, the agent file's model, CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL, then the main model. With none set it inherits the lead's model, so on a Fable session unlabelled helpers run on Fable.
Sub-agents do not share the parent's cache: each starts its own prefix. A fork inherits the parent's prefix and reads its cache. Up to 20 sub-agents run at once by default.

Claude Code's default effort is medium for Fable 5.2, Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5. The API defaults differ (high for Fable 5.2 and Sonnet 5.5). Thinking cannot be turned off on Fable 5.2 or Opus 5.5.

List prices per million tokens, input/output: Fable 5.2 $8/$40, Opus 5.5 $4/$20, Sonnet 5.5 $2/$10, Haiku 5.5 $0.10/$0.50 (five times higher above a 100K-token prompt). Cache reads: $0.20, $0.20, $0.10, a tenth of input.

Measured on one session at Fable list prices: cache reads were 91% of tokens but 7% of cost; cache writes 36% of cost; output including thinking 57%. One output token costs as much as 200 cached-input tokens on Fable 5.2.
Anthropic coding subset (463 problems): Opus 5.5 medium 93.1% at $0.22 per solved task; Opus high 95.5% at $0.30; Fable 5.2 low 94.6% at $0.39; Fable high 96.3% at $1.39.
Running low effort first and re-running only failures at high solved about 97% at about $0.17 per task, against 95.3% at $0.29 for everything at high: about 40% less cost for a higher pass rate.

On defect search, an Opus 5.5 lead with Sonnet 5.5 helpers scored 0.831 at $139 against Opus alone 0.850 at $236; a Fable 5.2 lead with Sonnet helpers scored 0.833 at $165, 19% more than the Opus lead.

Opus 5.5 at low effort scored 34 points below medium on an internal defect-search benchmark. Sonnet 5.5 on agentic coding went from 62.7% at medium to 77.8% at high. On deep research, Fable 5.2 high bought 3.2 points for 3.2 times the cost.

Anthropic measured agents using about 4 times the tokens of a chat and multi-agent systems about 15 times. Claude Code agent teams use about 7 times a standard session when teammates run in plan mode.
Fast mode gives up to 2.5 times faster output at twice the price, keeps a separate cache, and on subscription plans is billed from usage credits only. It works only on Fable and Opus models.

Fable 5.2 performs at about Opus 5.5's level on accelerator kernel optimisation and LLM architecture work, and declines most cybersecurity and research-biology tasks. In Claude Code a safety fallback leaves the session on the fallback model.

Hooks declared in a skill's frontmatter are registered when the skill is invoked and keep running for the rest of the session; once: true removes them after the first successful run. Agent hooks run only while that agent runs.

In Claude Code a model switch starts a fresh cache; an effort change keeps the cache on Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5 and Fable 5.1 or later with an API key or subscription, but not on Bedrock, Google Cloud, a gateway or under HIPAA settings. Spawning a sub-agent does not touch the parent's cache.

The skill listing in the system prompt is budgeted at 1% of the context window; past it, descriptions of the least-invoked skills are dropped first and names stay. Each description plus when_to_use is capped at 1,536 characters.
Haiku 5.5 is priced five times higher for prompts over 100K tokens (0.50 in, 2.50 out per million); Fable 5.2, Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 are flat up to 1M tokens.
On the deep-research benchmark high effort gains 3.3 points over low effort at 3.2 times the cost.
